instances.spoken_text: Consider a publisher. Enterprise value is six hundred million dollars. EBITDA of eighty million dollars grows twenty-five percent next year; forecast net income is fifty-five million dollars. What is the forward EV-to-EBITDA multiple?

follow_up.question: Why is forward EBITDA required here?
follow_up.reference: The requested multiple uses next year's operating earnings. Using the trailing figure would ignore the stated growth assumption and change the denominator.

instances.text: Consider a wholesaler. Enterprise value is 3.9 billion dollars. EBITDA of 120 million dollars grows 15 percent next year; forecast net income is 15 million dollars. What is the forward EV-to-EBITDA multiple?
instances.spoken_text: Consider a wholesaler. Enterprise value is three point nine billion dollars. EBITDA of one hundred and twenty million dollars grows fifteen percent next year; forecast net income is fifteen million dollars. What is the forward EV-to-EBITDA multiple?

follow_up.question: What if EBITDA growth were negative?
follow_up.reference: Positive enterprise value divided by lower positive EBITDA would produce a higher forward multiple. If forecast EBITDA reached zero or became negative, the usual positive-multiple interpretation would fail.
